name: socialLite
tagline: A lightweight tool for drafting, scheduling and cross-posting social media updates from one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part you actually see, a queue of posts with a calendar and a worker that fires them at the right minute, is a genuinely small build. The part that eats the weekend is every platform's API: OAuth app review, refresh token rotation, per-network media rules, rate limits, and the fact that some networks simply do not let a hobby app post on your behalf without an approved developer account. So you can get a personal scheduler running quickly and then spend days fighting paperwork you do not control. If you only post to one or two networks that have sane APIs, DIY is fine. If you need five networks, threads, analytics and a mobile composer, you are rebuilding a product, not a script.
coreLoopDIY: A local queue plus cron worker that takes a composed post with media and publishes it to your connected accounts at a scheduled time, with retries and a simple calendar view.
requirements: Developer accounts and approved API access on each network you want to post to
OAuth credentials stored in .env plus refresh token handling
An always-on host or scheduled job runner so posts fire when you are asleep
Object or local storage for images and video
whatYouLose: Pre-approved platform API access, which is the actual bottleneck and is not something code solves
Per-network preview, character limits and media transcoding handled for you
Mobile app or decent mobile composer for posting from a phone
Analytics, best-time suggestions and engagement pulled back into one view
Someone else repairing the integration the morning a network silently changes its API
moatNotes: The moat is not the scheduling logic, it is having approved developer status with every network and keeping it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Social APIs are hostile to small builders by design. Getting write access to a few of the big networks involves review queues, use-case justifications and occasional arbitrary rejection, and once you have it the terms and endpoints shift under you. Paying a few dollars a month to let someone else hold those credentials and fix them when they break is a rational trade, especially for anyone whose posting schedule is tied to actual revenue. The DIY build wins only for people posting to one or two developer-friendly networks who do not mind a queue that occasionally eats a post.
notes: Great weekend project right up to the moment a platform's developer portal asks you to record a screencast explaining your use case.
prompt:
Build a personal social media scheduler that runs on my own machine or a small VPS. No accounts, no multi-tenancy, no telemetry: single user, me.

Stack, no substitutions:
- SvelteKit with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/sociallite.db
- Tailwind for styling
- node-cron for the publish worker, running inside the same process
- Local disk storage for media at ./data/media

Features in scope:
1. Compose view: text area with live per-network character counters, image and video upload, and a datetime picker for scheduling.
2. Accounts: store OAuth access and refresh tokens per connected network in SQLite. Read client id and secret from .env. Implement the OAuth code flow for Mastodon first because it is the only one that works without a review process, and structure the adapter layer so other networks can be dropped in later.
3. Adapter interface: each network implements validate(post), upload(media), publish(post). Ship a working Mastodon adapter and a stub adapter that logs to console so the queue can be tested end to end.
4. Queue: posts table with status of draft, scheduled, publishing, published, failed. A cron job runs every minute, picks up due posts, publishes, retries up to three times with exponential backoff, and records the remote post URL or the error text.
5. Calendar view: month grid showing scheduled and published posts, click to edit a draft or scheduled post, delete cancels it.
6. Simple log page showing the last 100 publish attempts with status and error.

Out of scope, do not build: analytics, engagement metrics, inbox or reply handling, team approvals, AI copy generation, mobile app.

Deliverables: a README with exact setup steps, a .env.example listing every required variable, a seed script that inserts two sample scheduled posts against the stub adapter, and migrations applied automatically on boot. All secrets in .env, nothing hardcoded, no external services beyond the network APIs themselves.
